word.definition: A patina is a usually green film that forms on copper and bronze that is exposed to moist air for an extended time. The word patina can also refer to a shiny or dark surface that over time forms naturally on something (such as wood or leather), or to a literal or figurative thin layer.

sports_fact.text: Basketball at the 1936 Olympics was played outdoors on dirt courts. The gold-medal game was played in driving rain, and the US beat Canada 19-8.
